Subject: AWS Private Offer — usage vs. annual commitment, buyer gating & timeline

Hi Jessica,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great context on the pilot and expected token volumes. Per our conversation, I attached two term options (one that is annual committed-spinner and one that is usage-based with a 30% blended price floor for predictability). High-level differences:

- Annual commitment (12 months): ~20% lower unit price at typical scale; requires finance & procurement signoff + buyer PO for the full term; AWS private offer element is straightforward, but anything > $250k typically needs VP procurement approval on your side.
- Usage model (month-to-month): no long-term PO required, quicker to onboard to AWS Marketplace private offer, but per-unit pricing is higher and we use a modest monthly minimum to prevent churn.

Buyer approval gating we see commonly at Acme-size buyers: procurement forms + legal redline turnaround (usually 3–5 business days), cloud cost center signoff if they want to map to a central AWS account, and for annual commitments above your internal threshold a finance VP approval. If you want co-sell credit, AWS requires the buyer to accept the private offer and we need the co-sell registration filled out in parallel.

Next steps I propose:
1) Pick the preferred pricing path (usage vs annual).
2) If annual, send procurement the attached term sheet + we’ll generate marketplace private offer link and DocuSign envelope.
3) If usage, we open the private offer with a 30-day trial and a one-page PO template or card on file.

I attached the term comparison and pricing grid for your procurement team. If you want, Vanessa can join a short call with your procurement/legal to accelerate review — she’s copied.

Prep notes: we’ll need your procurement contact + their AWS Marketplace admin email to ensure buyer eligiblity on AWS.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Cloud GTM — Redwood Inference

Hello procurement team —

Forwarding the term options Jessica requested. For the usage-based private offer we typically include the following in the intake packet for procurement:

- One-page PO template (we can accept PO or card on file)
- Service description and SLA (99.9% inference service availability; token processing latency SLOs, and incident contact list)
- Data handling & residency note: customer data is not retained beyond inference session unless configured; we support US region private deployments and can add KMS/HSM details if required.
- Standard AWS Marketplace private offer flow + expected timeline:
  * If usage-based and no procurement redlines: we can create the private offer same-day and request buyer acceptance; acceptance to enable billing typically 24–72 hours.
  * If procurement requires redlines/DocuSign: add 3–7 business days for review + execution.

Internal note for Redwood ops (Vanessa/Marcus/Rishi) — please confirm the market-facing pricing SKU to attach to the private offer and whether we can lower the monthly minimum to $2k for Acme’s pilot to reduce friction. Vanessa, can you pre-fill the AWS listing console and start the private offer draft? Rishi / Marcus — flag any margin constraints if we shift the floor.

Regards,
Kimberly
